title: Ecclesiastes
summary: Ecclesiastes is a biblical book focused on wisdom, mortality, work, limits, joy under God, and the fear of the Lord.
historical_context: Ecclesiastes probes the limits of human striving and teaches wise reverence before God.
ancient_near_east_context: Ecclesiastes belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Ecclesiastes should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Ecclesiastes as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Wisdom Books, book 4 of 5, Ecclesiastes contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting wisdom, mortality, work, limits, joy under God, and the fear of the Lord to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Ecclesiastes as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Ecclesiastes uses wisdom within Wisdom Books, book 4 of 5 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Ecclesiastes helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional attribution to Solomon or wise circles
Many scholars see collected wisdom and later shaping
date_ranges: Later canonical shaping across the exilic or post-exilic period
original_audience: Israel's covenant community learning wise living under God
historical_setting: Royal, instructional, and reflective wisdom settings within Israel
canonical_role: Ecclesiastes anchors wisdom, mortality, work, limits, joy under God, and the fear of the Lord within Wisdom Books, book 4 of 5 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
structure: Conclusion and call to fear God
interpretive_disputes: How to read wisdom, lament, and reflection without flattening genre
